name: Dual VC Dimension
definition: For $\mathcal H\subseteq2^{\mathcal X}$, let $\mathcal H^*=\{x^*:x\in\mathcal X\}$ be the dual class on domain $\mathcal H$, where $x^*=\{h\in\mathcal H:x\in h\}$.  The **dual VC dimension** is $\mathrm{VC}^{*}(\mathcal H)=\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H^*)$.
graph_summary: The VC dimension after exchanging points and concepts: $\mathrm{VC}^{*}(\mathcal H)=\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H^*)$.
description: The shattering dimension of the transposed incidence matrix.
origin_references: The dual shatter function and its dimension are classical; the standard VC/dual-VC comparison is due to Assouad, \cite{assouad1983densite}.

monotonic.proof: If $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal G$, then $\mathcal H^*$ is a projection of $\mathcal G^*$ to the coordinates indexed by $\mathcal H$; VC dimension cannot increase under that projection.

p_monotonic.proof: A projection of $\mathcal H$ identifies some concepts. Its dual is a restriction of $\mathcal H^*$ to one representative of each resulting concept, so it cannot have larger VC dimension.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding inclusion and projection arguments establish both required monotonicities.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, and therefore follows from double monotonicity.
